note:
Round 2 of the /pages/shipping-returns banner, in the graphite register. Round 1 was briefed before Malcolm's note that the site's banners use the graphite branding style, so all 44 of its candidates are high-key - bright doorway, pale hallway - and off-brand for the same reason the contact wave was.

THE FORK THIS WAVE RESOLVES. The house graphite style is a seamless studio sweep (the-science, acetyl, copper-peptide, PDRN) and there are no doorways in a studio. Put to Malcolm 2026-08-30, who chose the DARK LOW-KEY REAL SCENE over a full studio sweep: keep the doorway and the hallway, but light them low-key against a near-black interior so the frame reads graphite in tone without pretending to be a studio. That is what `skin-concerns` already does on this site - a real scene lit dark, not a sweep - so there is precedent for both and this page takes the scene.

Why it is also the right call photographically: the key light is MOTIVATED. Daylight through the open door on the right is a real, hard source, and the hallway falling away to near-black on the left is what actually happens in that room. So the dark left 45 percent carrying the headline is not an invented void - it is the interior, correctly exposed for the door.

Compositions carried over from round 1, chosen by Malcolm: A (doorway), B (over the shoulder), D (wider threshold). C was dropped - he agreed it read closer to a product moment than a delivery.

⚠️ TWO WHITE OBJECTS NOW SIT IN A HARD KEY. Round 1 only had to keep the carton unprinted; low-key adds a second failure mode, which is the carton and the door frame clipping to flat paper-white and losing their edges. A blown carton stops reading as cardboard. Every slot says it holds detail and is never blown out, and 'clipped white' is negated.

The carton negatives from round 1 are kept in full and are still the main risk. A blank white box is the surface every engine wants to fill with a label, a barcode or a courier mark, and FLUX.2 prints characters unasked. Round 1 came back clean on all 44 at native pixels, checked with scripts/native-crop-qa.py - that check gets repeated here, on the chosen frame, before anything is uploaded.

⚠️ Luma is included per rule 1 but its output is NOT usable at this ratio: it snaps a 2.400:1 request to 2784x1504 = 1.851:1 on every slot. Composition reference only.

slots.title: A composition — doorway, low-key, hallway falling to near black
slots.prompt:
A photorealistic wide editorial photograph, 2.4:1 letterbox format, of a woman taking delivery of a parcel at the open door of her home, shot low-key with the interior in deep shadow.

The woman is in her late thirties with fair skin and dark shoulder-length hair, wearing a plain oatmeal knit jumper with no pattern. She stands on the right of the frame, her head and shoulders from about 0.56 to 0.80 of the frame width and from about 0.14 to 0.78 of the frame height, looking down at the parcel she is receiving with a warm, pleased, natural smile. Her face is in sharp focus and shows real, unretouched skin — visible pores, fine lines at the outer eye, faint natural colour variation.

She is taking a small square carton with both hands, flat palms supporting it from beneath, fingers relaxed and not wrapped over the top edge. Each hand has exactly five fingers, correctly proportioned. The carton sits from about 0.58 to 0.80 of the frame width and from about 0.60 to 0.90 of the frame height. It is plain matte white cardboard, completely blank and unprinted on every visible face — no label, no writing, no symbol, no barcode, no tape print, no mark of any kind. It holds its detail in the light: the top face is brighter than the front face and both edges between them stay visible, so it reads as cardboard. It is never blown out to flat paper-white.

At the right edge of the frame, nearest the camera, the delivery driver is seen only from behind: the back of his head and one shoulder, cropped by the right edge, entering from the bottom edge and reaching up to about 0.66 of the frame height and inward to about 0.96 of the frame width. Short dark hair, a plain slate-grey polo shirt that is completely unbranded — no logo, no printing, no badge, no name. He is soft, out of focus, and largely in shadow. No part of his face is visible at any point.

LIGHT: a single hard daylight source coming through the open doorway on the right, raking across her face and the carton and falling away fast. This is the only light in the picture — there is no lamp, no ceiling light and no fill from the interior. Her shadow side genuinely darkens.

GROUND: the hallway behind her, correctly exposed for that doorway light, so the interior sits in deep shadow and falls to near black toward the left edge and the top edge. The left 45 percent of the frame, measured from 0 to 0.45 of frame width, is that dark interior held at an even low tone with smooth continuous gradation and no visible edge, band, line, stripe or vignette ring anywhere, so a headline can sit on it unaided. It still reads as a real hallway with depth, not as a flat void, but nothing in it is identifiable — no furniture, no picture, no doorway beyond, no object carrying a character or symbol. It reaches the top, bottom and left edges of the frame.

Colour is near-black, deep warm grey, white and natural skin tones only. Shot on a full-frame camera with an 85mm lens at f/2.2, deep colour, natural, no filter, magazine-quality editorial photography.
